A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GLOBE and MP16-Reason research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GLOBE benchmark results, training-strategy and reward ablations, and qualitative model outputs in Tables 1–2 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and ablation results, supplemented by scene-specific evaluation, street-view testing, failure cases, efficiency measurements, and training reward trajectories.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 changes the localizability reward from an image-only classifier to an LLM-based model conditioned on both the image and generated reasoning. This makes a key reward candidate-dependent. Equation 5 also changes the advantage from mean-centered rewards to division by the group standard deviation. These revise the specified optimization procedure, although the PDFs do not establish implementation history.

E1.justification: v2 adds OSV-5M mini-3K as a dedicated street-view transfer evaluation beyond the retained MP16-Reason and IM2GPS3K benchmarks. This substantially extends the tested capture conditions and generalization scope. The newly documented geographic counts and indoor/nature/urban breakdowns describe existing MP16-Reason coverage rather than establishing a changed training dataset.

E2.justification: The main comparison changes from v1 Table 1 to v2 Table 2 by adding Hybrid, RFM-YFCC, InternVL3-8B, and Doubao1.5-VL, while removing G3 (LLaVA). These additions broaden the comparison across model families and capacities. GeoReasoner becoming GeoReasoner-7B is a matched naming clarification, not a new comparator.

E3.justification: v1 evaluates MP16-Reason using city/country label accuracy and IM2GPS3K at three distance thresholds. v2 uses five distance thresholds, from 1 to 2500 km, across benchmarks. New protocols include fixed-33K curation controls, an InternVL3-8B backbone comparison, and single-H20 efficiency tests varying streaming and concurrency. The original prompt and optimizer settings remain substantially unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained SFT and reward-component ablations, v2 adds a no-CoT control, backbone and data-curation ablations, and reward-weight sensitivity tests (Tables 3–5 and 11). It also adds scene-specific robustness, street-view transfer, two failure cases, efficiency analysis, and reward trajectories. The Boston qualitative comparison is retained and relocated, not newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. v2's reward curves have no uncertainty bands. The standard deviation newly introduced in the GRPO advantage is an algorithmic normalization term, not experimental uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 substantially expands results through new comparators, distance thresholds, ablations, OSV-5M evaluation, scene breakdowns, and efficiency measurements. MP16-Reason scores are replaced under different metrics and cannot establish before-and-after gains. GLOBE's shared IM2GPS3K scores remain 40.18, 56.19, and 71.45; Qwen2.5-VL-7B's 200/750 km entries change from 43.14/58.96 to 43.11/58.93.

T1.justification: Equation 1 revises the formal localizability definition to condition on generated reasoning. Equation 5 replaces reward centering with standardization and explicitly defines the group mean and standard deviation. These are substantive but localized mathematical revisions; neither version contains a theorem or proof development.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: MP16-Reason supplies diverse reasoning supervision, three task-specific rewards support GRPO training, and GLOBE offers interpretable, data-efficient geo-localization with strong open-source LVLM performance. Terminology edits and additional supporting experiments do not materially redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of multi-teacher bias reduction, student performance beyond its teachers, and dependence on backbone capacity and pretraining. Appendix A.2 distinguishes incorrect reasoning from plausible reasoning attributed to location-frequency bias and discusses the accuracy/latency tradeoff. Existing fine-grained localization limitations and privacy concerns are retained.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository link, exact dataset and geographic statistics, Microsoft Azure Maps geocoding instructions, H20 GPU allocations, vLLM deployment information, training throughput, and reward weights of 0.2/0.5/1. These materially improve documentation of previously unspecified choices. The existing prompt, training example, and optimizer hyperparameter table are retained; repository availability was not independently verified.

R1.justification: v2 adds targeted references covering visual place recognition, GeoRanker, generative geolocation, OSV-5M, multi-teacher distillation, and newer LVLMs. The introduction newly acknowledges retrieval's advantage at fine spatial precision. These broaden context without substantially changing the paper's positioning around reasoning-driven, data-efficient geo-localization.

P1.justification: Section 4.2 is substantially rewritten from dataset-benefit and model-strategy narratives into category-based baseline comparisons and organized reward, backbone, and curation ablations. A dedicated experimental-results appendix now organizes supplementary material. The revision also standardizes localizability and visual-cue terminology and updates affiliations, publication text, and acknowledgements.

P2.justification: v2 redesigns the main comparison and reward-ablation tables with five distance thresholds and clearer category groupings. It adds dataset-statistics, backbone, curation, scene, street-view, failure, efficiency, and weight-selection tables, plus training curves in Figure 6. The existing qualitative Figure 5 moves to Appendix A.2.5; it is not a new result display.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important validation gaps through fixed-size curation controls, a second backbone, and dedicated street-view transfer testing (Tables 4–5 and 8). The revised reward formulation removes v1's candidate-invariant localizability term, while additional implementation details, failure analysis, and efficiency measurements make the work more assessable and reproducible. Changed MP16-Reason metrics prevent direct accuracy comparisons, and repeated-run uncertainty remains absent. Nevertheless, the stronger validation and clearer specification constitute a substantial overall improvement.
